howToPlay.intro: Xiangqi (Chinese Chess) is a tactical mind game for two players. The ultimate goal is to checkmate or capture the opponent's <0>General</0>.
howToPlay.intro_p1: Xiangqi (Chinese Chess) is a tactical mind game for two players. The ultimate goal is to checkmate or capture the opponent's

section1.title: 1. The Board and Areas

river.label: River (He):
river.desc: Located in the middle, dividing the board into two parts. Some pieces (like Elephants) cannot cross the river.

palace.label: Palace (Jiu Gong):
palace.desc: A 3x3 square with diagonal lines on each side. The General and Advisors are only allowed to move within this area.

section1.boardDesc: The board consists of 10 horizontal lines and 9 vertical lines, pieces are placed on the intersections of the lines.

general.desc: Moves one square at a time, horizontally or vertically. Must stay within the Palace.
general.name: Tướng

advisor.desc: Moves one square diagonally. Must stay within the Palace.
advisor.name: Sĩ

elephant.desc: Moves 2 squares diagonally (X pattern). Cannot cross the river. Blocked if an intervening piece is present.
elephant.name: Tượng

horse.desc: Moves in an L shape. Blocked if there's a piece at the 'knee' of the L.
horse.name: Mã

chariot.desc: Moves horizontally or vertically any number of squares if not blocked.
chariot.name: Xe

cannon.desc: Moves like a Chariot. To capture, it must jump over exactly one piece (the 'mount').
cannon.name: Pháo

soldier.desc: Before crossing river, moves forward 1 square. After crossing, can move forward or sideways 1 square.
soldier.name: Tốt

section3.title: 3. Notation Differences Between Red and Black
section3.intro: While symmetric pieces have identical value and movement, the characters carved on them often differ to distinguish the 'Red' side from the 'Black' side.

meanings.advisor: Red: Civil Official / Black: Scholar Guard

why.title: Why are they different?
why.desc: This stems from simulating the Chu-Han Contention. Liu Bang (Han - Red) represents the court/legitimacy, Xiang Yu (Chu - Black) represents practical military power. Different characters also help players distinguish pieces easily on board setups.

elephantExample.title: Elephant Example (相/象)
elephantExample.desc: This pair is most confusing. Red is <0>相 (minister)</0>, Black is <1>象 (elephant)</1>. Both cannot cross the river as they are defensive protectors.
elephantExample.desc_p1: This pair is most confusing. Red is
elephantExample.desc_p5: Both cannot cross the river as they are defensive protectors.

soldier.name: Soldier
soldier.power: Values surges after crossing river in Endgame

kingFace.label: Facing Generals:
kingFace.desc: Generals cannot face each other on the same file without intermediary pieces.

check.label: Check:
check.desc: When a piece attacks the opponent's General.

mate.label: Checkmate:
mate.desc: When the General is under check with no way to escape.

opening.title: ⚔️ Opening Phase
opening.quote: "Chariots out early, Horses up later, Cannons flexible"
opening.desc: Prioritize deploying main pieces (Chariot, Cannon, Horse) to open positions. Common openings: Central Cannon vs Screen Horse, Same Direction Cannons.

midgame.title: 🛡️ Midgame Phase
midgame.desc: This is when battles break out. Focus on coordinating pieces to pressure the General or capture units. Always guard key files (4, 5, 6).

endgame.title: 🔚 Endgame Phase
endgame.desc: With few pieces left, Horse flexibility and Soldier strength are crucial. Master basic checkmates to finish the game.

tactics.title: 🔥 Checkmate Tactics
tactics.maHauPhao: Horse-then-Cannon mate: Using Horse as mount for Cannon.
tactics.thienDiaPhao: Heaven and Earth Cannons: Using two Cannons to control files/ranks.
tactics.daiDamXa: Bold Chariot: Driving Chariot straight into middle palace.

f1.a: A: No. In modern rules, you cannot repeat check attacks/states more than 3 times. Violations result in a loss.

f2.q: Q: Can the General leave the Palace?
f2.a: A: Absolutely not. General and Advisors are permanently restricted to the 3x3 area.

f3.q: Q: When is a match a Draw?
f3.a: A: A draw occurs when:<1 />1. <0>60-move rule:</0> 60 consecutive moves by each side without capture. Reset if any piece is captured.<2 />2. <0>Agreement:</0> Both players agree to draw.<3 />3. <0>Perpetual repetition:</0> Repeating a state 3 times (non-check).<4 />4. <0>Technical Draw:</0> Neither side has sufficient force to mate.
f3.a_item1_desc: 60 consecutive moves by each side without capture. Reset if any piece is captured.
f3.a_item4_desc: Neither side has sufficient force to mate.

f4.q: Q: Do I lose if I run out of time?
f4.a: A: Yes. When total match time expires (Timeout), that side loses immediately, regardless of board advantage.
f4.a_p1: A: Yes. When total match time expires (Timeout), that side loses immediately, regardless of board advantage.

history.title: Brief History of Xiangqi
history.p1: Xiangqi evolved from ancient Indian <0>Saturanga</0>, introduced to China and improved significantly. The board with River and Palace simulates the <1>Chu-Han Contention</1> between Liu Bang and Xiang Yu.
history.p2: Over thousands of years, it became a cultural staple in East Asia. In Vietnam, it's played everywhere from sidewalks to professional arenas.
history.p3: Today, playing online at <0>cotuong.xyz</0> connects millions of players, sharing passion and training thinking anytime, anywhere.

supplemental.title: In-depth Supplemental Knowledge
supplemental.p1: In xiangqi, understanding the board and piece positioning is the most important foundation. The Palace is not just where the General resides but also the primary target for the opponent.
supplemental.p2: When learning about {{title}}, pay attention to the coordination between pieces. Don't just look at a single piece; see how it protects or supports others to create a solid formation.
